paper.title: In-Situ Star Formation in the Outskirts of the Large Magellanic Cloud: Gaia DR2 Confirmation

extraction.summary: Paper studies six young B-type stars in the LMC outskirts. Two stars (390 and 403) are found to be likely LMC runaways and may escape the LMC, but the paper does not claim they are unbound from the Milky Way. The Milky Way orbit integration suggests they are not of Galactic origin. No stars are presented as Galactic-unbound hypervelocity star candidates.

method_chain.summary: Gaia DR2 (proper motions, parallaxes, photometry) and 2MASS J,H photometry are the primary data sources. The MB17 catalog (Moni Bidin et al. 2017) provides stellar ages, distances, and radial velocities for the six target stars.

we have opted to use 2MASS ... to photometrically select LMC members

method_chain.summary: Six young B-type main-sequence stars in the LMC outskirts previously identified by Moni Bidin et al. (2017, MB17). These are stars 292, 307, 390, 403, 405, and 406.

source_refs.context: In a recent contribution, Moni Bidin et al. (2017, MB17) presented a spectroscopic analysis of a set of candidate young, B-type, main-sequence stars in the outskirts of the LMC... MB17 found six stars...
We extract the proper motions for our six young stars from the Gaia DR2 catalog... The stars' IDs (Gaia DR2 and MB17) ... are listed in Table 1

method_chain.summary: Gaia DR2 coordinates for each field were matched with 2MASS using a 0.5 arcsec tolerance to combine 2MASS photometry with Gaia astrometry.

source_refs.context: Gaia DR2 coordinates in each field were matched with 2MASS, using a tolerance of 0.5 arcsec.

method_chain.summary: LMC membership selection: (1) 2MASS J,H color-magnitude box 12.5 ≤ J ≤ 15.5, 0.65 ≤ J‑H ≤ 1.0, (2) parallax cut (π − 2σ_π) ≤ 0, (3) manual trim of proper-motion outliers within each subfield.

source_refs.context: Our CMD cut is a box with 12.5 ≤ J ≤ 15.5 and 0.65 ≤ J‑H ≤ 1.0 ... These stars are further trimmed by distance, i.e., keeping those with parallaxes compatible with zero at 2σ_π level.
The mean proper motion within each subfield is determined from the JH-plus-parallax selected sample, after trimming proper-motion outliers by eye.

method_chain.summary: A fixed distance of 50 kpc is adopted for the LMC, based on the LMC distance modulus 18.49 (Pietrzyński et al. 2013). This distance is used to convert proper-motion differences to tangential velocities.

source_refs.context: Proper-motion differences are multiplied by a fixed 50-kpc distance, in agreement with the LMC's distance modulus of 18.49

method_chain.summary: Line-of-sight velocity differences (ΔV_los) relative to an LMC disk model are taken from Moni Bidin et al. (2017). These values are listed for comparison but not used in the travel distance calculations.

source_refs.context: For comparison, we also list in the last column of Tab. 2, the line-of-sight velocity difference ΔV_los between the target star and the prediction of an LMC disk model as determined in MB17. ΔV_los is not used in the determination of the travel distance.

method_chain.summary: Proper-motion differences (Table 1) are converted to tangential velocity differences (ΔV_T) using the fixed 50 kpc distance. Lifetime tangential travel distances are computed by multiplying ΔV_T by the MB17 stellar ages, expressed in both degrees and kpc.

source_refs.context: Proper-motion differences are multiplied by a fixed 50-kpc distance ... yielding velocities in the plane of the sky. The total tangential-velocity differences ... are listed in Table 2 as ΔV_T. Ages ... are combined to calculate lifetime tangential-travel distances ... in both degrees and kpc.

method_chain.summary: Solar position and motion parameters (R₀, z₀, V_circ, peculiar U,V,W) are not reported. The Milky Way orbit integration (step-12) presumably uses a standard solar motion, but no values are given.

source_refs.context: We integrate back in time the orbits of these two stars in an analytic 3-component Galactic potential (Johnston et al. 1995), using the distance moduli derived in MB17, and ignoring the LMC.

method_chain.summary: The Milky Way is represented by an analytic 3-component potential from Johnston, Spergel & Hernquist (1995). No parameters of the potential are stated.

source_refs.context: integrate back in time the orbits of these two stars in an analytic 3-component Galactic potential (Johnston et al. 1995)

method_chain.summary: Stars with ΔV_T > 200 km s⁻¹ at current LMC radii are claimed to escape the LMC, based on the results of Boubert et al. (2017, Fig. 4). This assessment applies to stars 390 and 403.

source_refs.context: The two stars with velocity differences in excess of 200 km s⁻¹ ... Thus, their likely origin is in the denser parts of the disk, having been ejected toward the outskirts. Their velocities in excess of 200 km s⁻¹ at current radii indicate that they escape the LMC (see e.g., Fig. 4 in Boubert+2017).

method_chain.summary: Conversion of observed positions, proper motions, radial velocities, and distance moduli to Galactocentric Cartesian positions and velocities, used as initial conditions for Milky Way orbit integration. The exact transformation is not detailed.

source_refs.context: We integrate back in time the orbits of these two stars in an analytic 3-component Galactic potential (Johnston et al. 1995), using the distance moduli derived in MB17, and ignoring the LMC.

method_chain.summary: Backward orbit integration is performed for stars 390 and 403 only, in the Milky Way potential (Johnston et al. 1995), ignoring the LMC. Pericenter distances and times are reported.

source_refs.context: To do so, we integrate back in time the orbits of these two stars in an analytic 3-component Galactic potential (Johnston et al. 1995), using the distance moduli derived in MB17, and ignoring the LMC. We find that the pericenter of star 390 is 49 kpc, ... For star 403, the predicted pericenter is 52 kpc ...

method_chain.summary: Stars 390 and 403 are classified as LMC runaways based on large travel distances and LMC escape velocities. Their Milky Way pericenters (~50 kpc) indicate they did not originate in the Galaxy; instead they likely escaped from the inner LMC, analogous to HVS3. The other four stars are consistent with in‑situ formation.

source_refs.context: The two stars with velocity differences in excess of 200 km s⁻¹ ... are moving away from the inner regions ... their likely origin is in the denser parts of the disk ... the remaining four stars appear to have formed locally.

Young stars with pericenters of ∼50 kpc are unlikely to have originated in our Galaxy. They more likely escaped from a more gas-rich region of the LMC, and are analagous to high-velocity star HVS3 that was recently confirmed to have a Magellanic origin.

candidate_groups_considered.description: Six young B-type main-sequence stars (MB17 IDs 292, 307, 390, 403, 405, 406) in the LMC outskirts, with Gaia DR2 proper motions. Studied to distinguish in‑situ formation from runaway origin.
candidate_groups_considered.reason: The paper does not present any of these stars as possibly unbound from the Milky Way. It only discusses LMC escape for stars 390 and 403, concluding they are LMC runaways. The Milky Way orbit integration indicates that 390 and 403 are unlikely to have originated in the Galaxy, and they are not claimed as Galactic hypervelocity star candidates.
